h: Shabbos Meals Bring Holiness Beyond the Manna

p: are called "the meals of the King."
And the saying of Chazal is known (Yoma 75b)
bread that the ministering angels eat;
Now at first glance, what is the wonder?
is called "the meal of the King,"
the holiness of the Shabbos meal
than the eating of the manna,
that the aspects of nefesh, ruach and neshamah
"and souls are hewn from the Throne,
and the nefesh from the Ofanim."
are the aspect of the world of Yetzirah,
which is half good and half evil,
which is the aspect of the Tree of Knowledge
is the aspect of the ruach in a person's heart,
where the heart of the wise is to his right
and the heart of the fool to his left;
and they are the two angels
and especially the desire for food;
for this was the serpent's counsel
"and she took of its fruit and ate";
וְהַלֵּב מִמֶּנּוּ תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים (מִשְׁלֵי ד, כג)
And "from the heart are the sources of life" (Mishlei 4:23):
so as not to be drawn
after the sense of his own pleasure,
with Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
as Rashi, of blessed memory, explains there.
And therefore our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said
And it says in the holy Zohar
"And the manna was like coriander seed":
take his portion across the Jordan?
So why did it single out only Gad?
that it is along the lines of the allusion
of our Rabbis, of blessed memory,
there has come the one who is destined
of the nations of the world;
and that is as our Sages, of blessed memory, said
he would have lived and endured forever, etc.;
and he lives and endures forever;
that is, that there was not found in him
of sensing the pleasure of this world.
the special quality of eating the manna:
from the sense of bodily pleasure.
And this was the complaint of the rabble,
"And now our souls are dried up;
even though they tasted in the manna
only because there was absent from them
the aspect of the desire for food
bread that the ministering angels eat:
in the aspect of an angel,
far from the desires of this world.
are from a place yet higher,
holiness is further added to the soul,
as our Sages, of blessed memory, said:
there is an addition of nefesh, ruach and neshamah
as it says in the holy Zohar:
that is, the aspect of the additional soul,
additional holiness comes to the soul
and that is "the meals of the King."
You have given to Your people";

p: And the matter of the rest of the Shabbos day
כִּי הוֹלֵךְ הָאָדָם אֶל בֵּית עוֹלָמוֹ
"For man goes to his eternal home":
since all his days he must
until he reaches his eternal home
prepared for him in the World to Come;
and then it is his place of rest.
with the affairs of this world,
and stand up for his soul
against his inclination that overpowers him,
as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Kiddushin 30b):
and were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him,
And when the Shabbos day comes,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him
and by this he will gather strength in his soul
in the six workdays after it,
until he merits to reach his rest.
Now at the time of the journeys
"They shall blow a teruah for their journeys";
for at the time of journeying and going,
which is the time of the war with the inclination,
a cry is born in the heart
to Hashem, may He be blessed;
"And when you go to war in your land
against the enemy who oppresses you,
you shall sound a teruah," etc.
And this is the matter of the cry
in the heart of the Jewish soul
one ceases work amid a tekiah,
because he senses rest in the soul,
And it says in the Gemara (Shabbos 35b):
"What shall we do about the Babylonians,
who cease work amid teruah sounds?"
the custom of their fathers is in their hands.
That is, the first exile to Bavel
with the craftsmen and the smiths,
at a time when there still was
the Beis HaMikdash standing in its place;
and when they came to Bavel
to the holiness they had sensed
when they were in their place in Eretz Yisrael,
from this the cry grew great in their souls,
and they would cease work amid the teruah.
in the holiness of the Shabbos day
as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Megillah 29a):
in the holiness of the Shabbos day.
And therefore we too cease work
because of the sense of rest.
And the people of Bavel too, now,
amid a tekiah after the Destruction,
the custom of their fathers is in their hands,
